option_description: Whether every sensitive flow traverses TLS (or an equivalent encrypted tunnel such as IPsec) with no reachable cleartext/plaintext path — HTTP redirected to HTTPS, database and internal service links also encrypted.
security_impact: Satisfies "TLS enforced on all flows (no cleartext fallback)" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when tls_only_transport is true (alongside insecure_transport_denied). When this protection is present the countermeasure mitigates network sniffing of cleartext traffic and AiTM interception (ATT&CK M1041 Encrypt Sensitive Information, D3FEND D3-ET Encrypted Tunnels).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm a plaintext HTTP request to the host is redirected to HTTPS rather than served in the clear.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: 301/308 redirect to an https:// URL (secure) — a 200 served over plain HTTP, or any sensitive content returned without redirect, is insecure
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Transport Layer Security Cheat Sheet

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm TLS is offered on the service port and the plaintext path is closed; for internal/DB flows confirm the encrypted listener is the only one reachable.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: TLS offered on the service port and the plaintext path closed; for internal/DB flows confirm the encrypted listener is the only one reachable
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Transport Layer Security Cheat Sheet

how_to_obtain.instruction: For object-store flows, confirm TLS is required (not merely available) via the bucket transport policy.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A bucket policy Deny on aws:SecureTransport=false (AWS Security Hub control S3.5 PASSED) — confirms TLS is required, not merely available
how_to_obtain.source: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark (Security Hub control mapping)

option_description: Whether cleartext/plaintext fallback is denied — bare HTTP refused or redirected to HTTPS, no opportunistic downgrade, no permitted unencrypted fallback for protected flows.
security_impact: Satisfies "TLS enforced on all flows (no cleartext fallback)" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when insecure_transport_denied is true (alongside tls_only_transport). Present means no unencrypted fallback remains for an on-path attacker to force, mitigating cleartext sniffing (ATT&CK M1041, D3FEND D3-ET).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm a plaintext HTTP request is refused or redirected rather than serving content over the clear channel.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: 301/308 redirect to an https:// URL (secure) — a 200 served over plain HTTP, or any sensitive content returned without redirect, is insecure
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Transport Layer Security Cheat Sheet

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the plaintext listener is closed and only the TLS listener is reachable on the protected port.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: TLS offered on the service port and the plaintext path closed; for internal/DB flows confirm the encrypted listener is the only one reachable
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Transport Layer Security Cheat Sheet

how_to_obtain.instruction: For object-store flows, confirm a policy actively denies non-TLS requests rather than merely supporting TLS.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A bucket policy Deny on aws:SecureTransport=false (AWS Security Hub control S3.5 PASSED) — confirms cleartext is denied, not merely TLS-capable
how_to_obtain.source: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark (Security Hub control mapping)

option_description: The minimum negotiable TLS version. Secure posture is TLS 1.2 floor with TLS 1.3 preferred; SSLv2/SSLv3/TLS 1.0/TLS 1.1 (deprecated by RFC 8996) are disabled.
security_impact: Satisfies "Minimum TLS version enforced (TLS 1.2 floor, 1.3 preferred)" — firing when min_tls_version equals tls1_2_or_higher. Enforcing the floor blocks protocol-downgrade attacks (POODLE/legacy-class), mitigating ATT&CK T1562-style downgrade (D3FEND D3-ET).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Enumerate the protocol versions the service accepts and confirm no deprecated version is offered.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Only TLSv1.2 and/or TLSv1.3 sections present; any SSLv3 / TLSv1.0 / TLSv1.1 section listed is insecure
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Transport Layer Security Cheat Sheet

how_to_obtain.instruction: Actively attempt a deprecated-version handshake and confirm the server rejects it.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Handshake FAILS / connection refused for tls1_1 (and -ssl3, -tls1) = secure; a successful handshake on a deprecated version is insecure
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-52 Rev. 2 — Guidelines for the Selection, Configuration, and Use of TLS Implementations

option_description: The cipher-suite policy. Secure posture offers only AEAD suites with forward secrecy (GCM/ChaCha20-Poly1305 over ECDHE/DHE); legacy CBC/RC4/3DES/NULL/anonymous/EXPORT/static-RSA suites are disabled.
security_impact: Satisfies "Strong forward-secret AEAD cipher suites only" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when cipher_suites_strong_only equals aead_with_forward_secrecy_only (alongside perfect_forward_secrecy_enabled). Present removes weak/broken-cipher exploitation (RC4/Sweet32/NULL/EXPORT), mitigating ATT&CK M1041.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Enumerate accepted cipher suites and confirm only forward-secret AEAD suites are offered with no weak suites present.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Only GCM/CHACHA20-POLY1305 ECDHE/DHE (forward-secret AEAD) suites listed with strength 'A'; presence of RC4/3DES/NULL/EXPORT/anon = insecure
how_to_obtain.source: Mozilla Server Side TLS (Intermediate & Modern configurations)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm no weak/insecure cipher findings and that forward secrecy is reported for all offered suites, per protocol.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No weak/insecure cipher findings; forward secrecy reported for all offered suites
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Transport Layer Security Cheat Sheet

option_description: Whether ephemeral (ECDHE/DHE) key exchange is enabled so compromise of a long-term key cannot decrypt past recorded sessions.
security_impact: Satisfies "Strong forward-secret AEAD cipher suites only" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when perfect_forward_secrecy_enabled is true (alongside cipher_suites_strong_only). Present ensures recorded traffic stays unreadable after key compromise, mitigating store-now-decrypt-later sniffing (ATT&CK M1041).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the negotiated/offered suites use ephemeral ECDHE/DHE key exchange (forward secrecy) for every protocol.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No weak/insecure cipher findings; forward secrecy reported for all offered suites
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Transport Layer Security Cheat Sheet

how_to_obtain.instruction: Cross-check via the cipher enumeration that all listed suites are ECDHE/DHE-based rather than static-RSA key exchange.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Only GCM/CHACHA20-POLY1305 ECDHE/DHE (forward-secret AEAD) suites listed with strength 'A'; presence of any non-forward-secret static-RSA suite is insecure
how_to_obtain.source: Mozilla Server Side TLS (Intermediate & Modern configurations)

option_description: Whether the client performs full peer-certificate validation: chain to a trusted CA, hostname match in subjectAlternativeName, within validity, adequate key (RSA>=2048/ECDSA P-256), SHA-256 signature — not skipped.
security_impact: Satisfies "Server certificate validated (trusted chain + hostname)" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when server_certificate_validated is true (alongside tls_root_trust_managed). Present defeats certificate spoofing via invalid-cert acceptance and AiTM substitution (ATT&CK T1557, D3FEND D3-CERO).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Open a verified TLS connection with hostname (SNI) and confirm the chain validates and the certificate matches the host.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: 'Verify return code: 0 (ok)' and the CN/SAN matches the host = secure; 'self signed certificate' / 'certificate has expired' / verify error = insecure
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-52 Rev. 2 — Guidelines for the Selection, Configuration, and Use of TLS Implementations

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the presented certificate's validity dates, SAN, key size and signature algorithm for adequacy.
how_to_obtain.command: echo | openssl s_client -connect <host>:<port> 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -dates -subject -ext subjectAltName -text | grep -E 'Public-Key|Signature Algorithm'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: notAfter in the future, SAN contains the FQDN, Public-Key >= 2048 bit (RSA) or P-256 (EC), Signature Algorithm sha256 — anything weaker is insecure
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Transport Layer Security Cheat Sheet

option_description: Whether the trusted-CA root store is curated and actively maintained — no rogue, expired, or unnecessary root CAs.
security_impact: Satisfies "Server certificate validated (trusted chain + hostname)" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when tls_root_trust_managed is true (alongside server_certificate_validated). A curated trust store ensures validation rests only on legitimate anchors, mitigating cert spoofing (ATT&CK T1557, D3FEND D3-CERO).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the client/host trust store for unexpected, expired, or rogue root CAs and confirm a maintenance process governs additions and removals.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Trust store contains only expected, in-date roots from a maintained list; any unknown, expired, or organisation-injected rogue root CA is a finding
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

how_to_obtain.instruction: Enumerate the system trust store and check each root's validity dates, looking for expired or unexpected anchors.
how_to_obtain.command: trust list --filter=ca-anchors 2>/dev/null || awk -v cmd='openssl x509 -noout -subject -enddate' '/BEGIN/{c=""} {c=c $0 ORS} /END/{print c | cmd; close(cmd)}' /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Each listed anchor is an expected, in-date root CA; expired notAfter dates or unrecognised issuers indicate an unmanaged or compromised trust store
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Whether mutual TLS (client-certificate authentication) is enforced on flows that require it — service-to-service, internal east-west, privileged API — so the client is authenticated, not only the server.
security_impact: Satisfies "Mutual TLS / client authentication where required" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when service_to_service_mtls_enforced is true (alongside peer_authentication_mtls_mode_strict). Present authenticates both peers, mitigating unauthenticated-peer access on sensitive flows (D3FEND D3-ET).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the server requests a client certificate (CertificateRequest) on flows that require mutual authentication.
how_to_obtain.command: openssl s_client -connect <host>:<port> </dev/null 2>&1 | grep -i 'Acceptable client certificate CA names\|request'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Server sends a CertificateRequest (lists acceptable client CA names) on mTLS-required flows; a flow that needs client auth but never requests a client cert is insecure
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-52 Rev. 2 — Guidelines for the Selection, Configuration, and Use of TLS Implementations

how_to_obtain.instruction: Positively test that a connection without a client certificate is rejected on the mTLS-required flow.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Connection without a client cert is refused (handshake failure / certificate required alert) = secure; a completed handshake with no client cert means mTLS is not enforced
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Whether mTLS peer-authentication runs in STRICT mode (no permissive plaintext fallback) with per-server TLS session-cache scoping so session reuse cannot bypass per-host client-cert checks (cf. CVE-2025-23419).
security_impact: Satisfies "Mutual TLS / client authentication where required" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when peer_authentication_mtls_mode_strict is true (alongside service_to_service_mtls_enforced). Present closes the TLS session-reuse client-cert bypass (CVE-2025-23419, D3FEND D3-ET) and forbids permissive cleartext fallback.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm peer authentication is STRICT and the TLS session cache is scoped per server so a session from one virtual server cannot be reused against another to bypass client-cert auth.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Confirm TLS session-cache is scoped so a session from one virtual server cannot be reused against another to bypass client-cert auth (cf. CVE-2025-23419); patch nginx >= 1.27.4/1.26.3
how_to_obtain.source: CVE-2025-23419 — nginx TLS session-reuse client-cert authentication bypass

how_to_obtain.instruction: For a service mesh (e.g. Istio), confirm the PeerAuthentication mTLS mode is STRICT rather than PERMISSIVE.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: mtls.mode is STRICT for the protected namespaces/workloads; PERMISSIVE (which still accepts plaintext) is insecure
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: The downgrade and renegotiation posture: TLS_FALLBACK_SCSV honoured (no forced fallback / downgrade sentinel absent) and only secure RFC 5746 renegotiation permitted.
security_impact: Satisfies "Downgrade & renegotiation protection + HSTS" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when downgrade_and_renegotiation_protected equals downgrade_sentinel_absent_and_secure_renegotiation_only (alongside hsts_enabled). Present blocks protocol/cipher downgrade attacks (ATT&CK T1562, D3FEND D3-ET).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Force a fallback handshake with TLS_FALLBACK_SCSV and confirm the server rejects the downgrade.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Server rejects the downgraded fallback handshake (inappropriate fallback alert) = secure; a successful forced-downgrade is insecure
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Transport Layer Security Cheat Sheet

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check that the server reports secure renegotiation support and refuses insecure client-initiated renegotiation.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure (RFC 5746) renegotiation supported and insecure / client-initiated renegotiation refused (DoS-safe) = secure; insecure renegotiation allowed is insecure
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Whether a Strict-Transport-Security header is returned with an adequate max-age so browsers never fall back to HTTP for protected origins.
security_impact: Satisfies "Downgrade & renegotiation protection + HSTS" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when hsts_enabled is true (alongside downgrade_and_renegotiation_protected). Present prevents browser HTTP fallback / SSL-strip downgrade (ATT&CK T1562, D3FEND D3-ET).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Fetch the response headers and confirm the Strict-Transport-Security header is present with a long max-age.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload present (a long max-age, ideally 2 years) = secure; header absent = insecure
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP HTTP Strict Transport Security Cheat Sheet

option_description: Whether certificates are issued and rotated before expiry through an automated/governed process (ACME/cert-manager/managed service) with adequate key sizes — not long-lived hand-managed certs that silently expire.
security_impact: Satisfies "Managed certificate lifecycle (rotation, key size, not expired)" — one of its OR-conditions — firing when certificate_lifecycle_managed is true. Present prevents expiry-gap cert spoofing and outage, mitigating certificate-spoofing-via-invalid-cert acceptance (D3FEND D3-CERO Certificate Rotation/Revocation).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the live certificate's expiry to confirm it is comfortably in-date and on a short renewal cadence.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: notAfter date comfortably in the future and on a short renewal cadence (~90 days lifetime per Mozilla) = secure; long-lived or near-expiry = lifecycle gap
how_to_obtain.source: Mozilla Server Side TLS (Intermediate & Modern configurations)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm an automated renewal mechanism and a documented rotation runbook are in place; for IPsec/non-TLS flows confirm IKE rekey and approved crypto.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Evidence of automated renewal (ACME/cert-manager/managed cert service) and a rotation runbook; for IPsec/non-TLS flows confirm IKE rekey + approved crypto (AES-GCM, SHA-256+, ECDH/X25519)
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-77 Rev. 1 — Guide to IPsec VPNs

option_description: The maximum certificate validity period in days; <=398 is the secure short-cadence threshold (shorter, e.g. ~90 days per Mozilla, is preferred).
security_impact: Satisfies "Managed certificate lifecycle (rotation, key size, not expired)" — its second OR-group — firing when certificate_max_validity_days is <= 398. A bounded lifetime limits exposure of a compromised key and forces regular rotation (D3FEND D3-CERO Certificate Rotation/Revocation).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the certificate's notBefore and notAfter and compute the validity span to confirm it does not exceed 398 days.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: The span between notBefore and notAfter is <= 398 days (ideally ~90) = secure; a longer validity period is a lifecycle gap
how_to_obtain.source: Mozilla Server Side TLS (Intermediate & Modern configurations)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the issuance policy / CA profile caps the maximum certificate lifetime at or below 398 days.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Issuance policy or ACME/CA profile documents a maximum lifetime of <= 398 days; profiles allowing multi-year certs are a finding
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge
